newsitem.title: UK: Versalite plans market debut and new product sales.
newsitem.headline: Versalite plans market debut and new product sales.

text.p: Versalite Group Plc, a maker of decorated glass products, said on Monday it was planning to float on the London Stock Exchange on May 14 and would use the proceeds to finance the expansion of sales of new products.
Versalite said it had raised 800,000 stg, net of expenses, via a placing at three pence per share.
The market capitlisation of Versalite will be 4.32 million stg, based on the issue price.
The group recently developed a lower-cost method of producing its principal product, a coloured decorated flat glass marketed under the name of Versalite.

Versalite said previous production of the glass involved a two-stage water slide transfer process but it now requires only one stage which significantly reduces the cost of Versalite and opens up new markets for the product.

Sales and Marketing Director Nicholas Easton said the most exciting development was the introduction of a new machine that automatically applies heat release transfers which will enable Versalite to be mass-produced economically for the first time.
"We consider this to be a major breakthrough," Easton said.

The group said the mass production of Versalite and the consequent reduction in cost will open new markets for such products as shower screens, ceramic hobs, amusement and gaming machine fronts, cooker panels and microwave fronts as well as expanding the existing demand for coloured decorative glass which has been mainly used for architectural cladding.
